title: The fixed rule on net1 v6, validation links: the u grid over three campaign seeds
description: net1 v6 (exp-net1v6-149, seed 0, chosen there) is net1 v5's settings trained on v5's data plus wider ranges (exp-data-net1-v6-146). It replaces v5 by the choice rule in experiments/net1v6.json: inside v5's ranges (exp-net1v6-inrange-152) its CRPS skill is no lower (validation 0.776 to 0.777 against 0.774, test 0.782 to 0.784 against 0.778) and its calibration no worse (mean |coverage - 0.9| 0.033 to 0.035 against 0.033), and on every held-out set its coverage is as close to 0.9 or closer (8 to 16 BDP buffers 0.06 against 0.09, 151 to 250 ms 0.12 against 0.19). The rule asked for the log score; v6's bins are wider than v5's inside v5's ranges, which lowers its log loss by construction, so the bin-free CRPS stands in for it. The fixed rule's u is chosen again on v6 exactly as it was on v5 (rule-net1v5-val.json): u in -0.25, 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, with BBRv3, on the 21 validation links and five families, for campaign seeds 11, 21 and 31; the winner is the u with the highest mean over the five families on every seed, or, where seeds disagree or the gap is inside the noise, the one ahead on the mean over seeds. Validation links only.
prepare: N="$IN/v6/net1-v6-s0/net1.pt"; U="-0.25 0 0.125 0.25 0.375 0.5"; uv run python experiments/rule_export.py "$OUT/v6" "$N" --u $U; P=(); for u in $U; do P+=(--policy "v6-u$u=$OUT/v6/rule-u$u.onnx"); done; for s in 11 21 31; do mkdir -p "$OUT/s$s"; experiments/rule_eval.sh "$OUT/s$s" val $s $s bbr3 "${P[@]}"; done
run: for c in "$OUT"/s*/c-*; do uv run expliccit campaign run "$c" --shard "$SHARD/$SHARDS" --build "$UML" --workers "$WORKERS" --tables steps; done
collect: for s in 11 21 31; do uv run python experiments/rule_report.py "$OUT/s$s" --select v6; done; { for s in 11 21 31; do echo "# Campaign seed $s"; cat "$OUT/s$s/summary.md"; echo; done; } > "$OUT/summary.md"
